sentence.text: In each location where information, goods or services are provided to the public at service counters in buildings of assembly occupancy, at least one of the service counters shall be equipped with (See .)

sentence.text: Exterior walks that form part of an accessible path of travel shall

clause.text: have a slip-resistant, continuous and even surface,
be not less than 1 600 mm wide,
have a level area conforming to adjacent to an entrance doorway, and
be designed in accordance with Clause 8.2.1 of CSA B651, “Accessible design for the built environment.”

sentence.text: Except when designed as a curb ramp in accordance with Clause 3.8.3.4.(1)(b), a ramp located in an accessible path of travel shall

clause.text: have a clear width not less than 1 000 mm (see ),
have a uniform slope along its length not more than 1 in 12 (see ),

have a level area not less than 1 700 mm by 1 700 mm at the top and bottom and at intermediate levels of a ramp leading to a door, so that on the latch side the level area extends not less than (see ),

subclause.text: 600 mm beyond the edge of the door opening where the door opens towards the ramp, or
300 mm beyond the edge of the door opening where the door opens away from the ramp,

clause.text: have a level area not less than 1 350 mm long and at least the same width as the ramp

subclause.text: at intervals not more than 9 m along its length, and
where there is an abrupt change in the direction of the ramp, and

sentence.text: Except as provided in and except for a door with a power door operator complying with , when unlatched, a door in an accessible path of travel shall open when the force applied to the handle, push plate or latch-releasing device is not more than

clause.text: 38 N in the case of an exterior swinging door,
22 N in the case of an interior swinging door, or
22 N in the case of a sliding door.

sentence.text: Except for a door at the entrance to a dwelling unit, a closer for an interior door in an accessible path of travel shall have a closing period of not less than 3 s measured from when the door is in an open position of 70° to the doorway, to when the door reaches a point 75 mm from the closed position, measured from the leading edge of the latch side of the door. (See .)

Unless equipped with a power door operator complying with , a swinging door in an accessible path of travel shall have a clear space on the latch side extending the height of the doorway and not less than (See Note A-3.8.3.6.(11).)

clause.text: 600 mm beyond the edge of the door opening if the door swings toward the approach side, and
300 mm beyond the edge of the door opening if the door swings away from the approach side.

sentence.text: A vestibule located in an accessible path of travel shall be arranged to allow the movement of wheelchairs between doors and shall provide a distance between 2 doors in series of not less than 1 350 mm plus the width of any door that swings into the space in the path of travel from one door to another.
Only the active leaf in a multiple-leaf door in an accessible path of travel need conform to the requirements of this Article.

Except as provided in and , the clear floor space on the pull side of a swinging door in an accessible path of travel shall be level within a rectangular area of not less than 1 700 mm by 1 500 mm measured from the hinged side of the door. (See .)

Except for facilities for persons with cognitive disabilities such as dementia, doorways leading from a public corridor or a corridor used by the public that provide access to a public area or an exit shall be provided with a door or door frame that has a readily apparent visual contrast with adjacent wall surfaces. (See .) (See also Note A-3.4.6.11.(4).)
